title: The save and cancel controls at the foot of every journey page send the user back to "the hub"; Design release 1 calls the same page the overview

finding.frontend: Every journey page ends with the same three controls, built by one shared macro (src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13): a primary "Save and continue" button, a secondary "Save and return to hub" button and a "Cancel and return to hub" link. The wording comes from src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:42-45. Both strings appear on 41 of the 67 captured frontend screens. The page they name is headed "Overview", so the word "hub" appears nowhere the user can see it except on these two controls — it is the internal name for the task list.
finding.prototype: Design release 1 uses the same three-control pattern with the same primary label, and names the destination after what it is headed: "Save and return to overview" and "Cancel and return to overview" (app/views/consignment-details.html:145). Both strings appear on 29 of the 60 captured screens.
finding.difference: Rename saveAndReturnToHub to "Save and return to overview" and cancelAndReturnToHub to "Cancel and return to overview" in src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:42-45. Both keys are read only by src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13, so one edit changes every page. The three controls and their order do not move, and the key names themselves can stay as they are; only the strings are user-visible. The primary button beside them, however, does not always agree, and this rename does not touch it: on seven captured frontend screens the primary reads "Continue" where the Design release 1 screen it pairs with reads "Save and continue" — the three consignment-addresses hub states (fe-addresses-hub, -empty and -complete, against dr1-roles-and-addresses and dr1-roles-and-addresses-answered) and the four documents states (fe-documents, -populated, -scanning and -error, against the dr1-upload-documents family). It is not a blanket difference: on check-your-answers and on the declaration both sides read "Continue", so the two designs agree there. That primary label does not come from src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:42-45 and is not read by src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13 — each of those pages passes its own — so it is a different edit in different files and it is recorded here as an observation rather than folded into this rename.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding the word "hub" in a button or link label in the captured DOM of any Design release 1 screen, or "overview" in one on the frontend side.
finding.verification: Ran the falsifier both ways. "hub" appears in 33 prototype files but never inside an element's text — extracting every >…hub…< run across the 60 files returns nothing, so all 33 are hrefs and form values such as /notification-hub and value="hub". "Overview" appears on the frontend only as fe-hub.html's <title> and its h1 at line 106, never as a button or link label. Counted the strings: "Save and return to hub" and "Cancel and return to hub" are each on 41 of the 67 frontend files, "Save and return to overview" and "Cancel and return to overview" on 29 of the 60 prototype files. Read src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13 and src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:42-45, and app/views/consignment-details.html:138-152, where line 145 is the "Save and return to overview" button and the cancel link follows it. Opened evidence/frontend@76a864ba/page/fe-origin.png for the rendered three-control group.
finding.correction: The copy claim is correct and the slot is unchanged, but the prototype slot's opening — "Design release 1 uses the same three-control pattern" — is true only of the 29 screens that carry it. Comparing the two sets against pairs.cjs, five frontend page groups render the secondary button and the cancel link where the Design release 1 page they pair with shows a single primary button and no cancel: origin, cph-number, contact address, transporter type against dr1-transporter-add, and private transporter. That is a difference in whether the pattern appears at all rather than in what it says, so it is recorded as its own finding, service-wide--save-and-cancel-shown-where-the-design-shows-one-button, and this one is left to the wording alone. A SECOND CORRECTION, MADE BY THE CORPUS EDITOR IN A PRE-INGEST EDIT PASS AND NOT BY THE VERIFIER ABOVE. What was claimed: the difference slot ended "Nothing else about the pattern moves — the three controls, their order and 'Save and continue' already agree." What is true: the primary button's label does not always agree. On seven captured frontend screens it reads "Continue" where the Design release 1 screen it pairs with reads "Save and continue". How it was checked: grepped the captured frontend DOM for a button label of exactly "Continue" and got twelve files — the three consignment-addresses hub states, the four documents states, the three check-your-answers states and the two declaration states. Read the primary button out of each one's paired Design release 1 capture, taking the pairs from pairs.cjs rather than guessing them. capture/html/frontend/fe-addresses-hub.html:198-203 renders "Continue" as the primary with "Save and return to hub" beneath it, while its pair capture/html/prototype/dr1-roles-and-addresses.html:346-361 renders "Save and continue", "Save and return to overview" and "Cancel and return to overview" — so the two secondary controls this finding renames sit under a primary that already disagrees. fe-addresses-hub-complete.html:200 and fe-addresses-hub-empty.html:189 are the same. The four documents states pair with the dr1-upload-documents family, whose primary is "Save and continue" at capture/html/prototype/dr1-upload-documents.html:541. The other five of the twelve are not differences: dr1-review-notification.html:1142 and dr1-declaration.html:320 both read "Continue", matching the frontend's check-your-answers and declaration pages. Why the verifier missed it: the counter-examples are all on screens belonging to other slices, and this finding's own screens are fe-consignment-details and dr1-consignment-details, where the primary does agree. The difference slot now states the seven screens and says explicitly that the primary label is out of scope of this rename, because it comes from each page's own copy rather than from the shared keys this finding changes. The rename itself is untouched and still correct.

relatedTo.why: Both change the same three controls at the foot of a journey page — one what they say, the other which pages they appear on.
